name: Slovenia
tagline: Free tuition for EU students, but very few English bachelor's
summary: Slovenia is cheap, safe and free: as an EU citizen you pay no tuition for full-time bachelor study, exactly like a Slovenian. The catch is blunt - almost all bachelor teaching is in Slovene. The four public universities list about seventeen English-taught bachelor's between them, most of them at Primorska and Maribor, and the University of Ljubljana's one was open only to non-EU applicants in 2026. If one of those programmes is what you want, you pay no tuition, and a dormitory room, if you can get one, costs EUR 80-250 a month. If not, it is not an option.
whyConsider: Full-time bachelor tuition is free for EU/EEA citizens - the same deal Slovenian students get
Living costs are genuinely low: a student dorm room is EUR 120-250 a month and a student meal costs you about EUR 4.37
One central application portal, eVS, handles everything including the recognition of your IB Diploma
University of Primorska in Koper has ten English-taught bachelor's, including mathematics, computer science and bioinformatics
Ljubljana is small, walkable and an hour from both the Alps and the Adriatic
watchOuts: English-taught bachelor's are very thin: 10 at Primorska, 5 at Maribor, 1 at Nova Gorica, and 1 at Ljubljana that the 2026 call opened only to non-EU applicants
Private international students are generally not eligible for university dormitories except in Maribor - dorms are reserved for exchange and scholarship students
IB-specific minimum points and a mapping onto the Slovenian Matura are not confirmed here; ask the ENIC-NARIC Centre or the faculty directly

Whether your IB Diploma needs a formal recognition procedure depends on which official page you read, and the two do not agree - see the recognition notes. Do not assume either answer without getting it in writing.
Some published non-EU fee figures are old (Primorska's range is labelled 2021/2022), so treat fee pages with suspicion
Applying is not enrolling. Slovenia decides the first round on 24 July and expects you to enrol at the faculty by mid-August, and both of those dates land inside the Danish summer holidays.

notes: Two official Slovenian pages disagree about whether an IB Diploma needs a formal recognition procedure (priznavanje), so do not assume the more comfortable answer.

The University of Ljubljana’s own Slovene admission leaflet for 2026 says it is not needed: "Diploma o mednarodni maturi (International Baccalaureate - IB) in zakljucno spricevalo Evropske mature (European Baccalaureate Certificate) sta enakovredna maturitetnemu spricevalu v RS in zanju ni potreben postopek priznavanja tujega izobrazevanja." The same paragraph says the exemption is for the Diploma: "Kandidati z IB certifikatom morajo dokazila prilozit sami in tudi opraviti postopek priznavanja izobrazevanja" - a candidate holding IB certificates rather than the full Diploma does have to run the procedure.

The national Study in Slovenia portal states the obligation flatly and names no exemption at all: a candidate who finished school abroad "is obliged to acquire a decision on the recognition of the foreign education, if they have not obtained one already". It does not mention the International Baccalaureate anywhere.

Read together, the most likely reading is that the leaflet states a specific exemption the national portal simply does not mention. That is the convenient reading, which is exactly why it should not be relied on: get it in writing from the faculty, or from recognition@uni-lj.si, before you plan around it. If recognition does turn out to be required, the leaflet warns a decision can take up to two months from a complete application, and the first-round selection on 24 July only covers candidates whose recognition decision has already been issued.

The higher education institutions themselves are the competent bodies for the recognition procedure. The Slovenian ENIC-NARIC Centre, inside the Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Innovation, is the national information point (enic-naric@gov.si, +386 1 478 46 00). Where recognition is required the application is submitted together with the study application through the eVS portal.

IB-specific minimum points, an HL/SL mapping onto the Slovenian Matura and a grade conversion table are not confirmed here. Contact the ENIC-NARIC Centre and the specific faculty before you rely on anything here.

For domestic applicants the access requirement is the Matura, a final examination taken before 1 June 1995, or a vocational Matura plus an additional general Matura subject. How an IB Diploma is scored against this for capped programmes is not documented publicly.

deadlines.label: Joint call for enrolment (skupni razpis za vpis) published — until it is out, your cycle has no deadlines
deadlines.year: 2027/2028 entry — the 2027/2028 call was still not published on 2026-09-24
deadlines.notes: Precedent: the government approved the 2026/2027 joint call on 29 January 2026 and the ministry published it on 30 January 2026 — the University of Ljubljana leaflet dates it "MVZI, 30. januar 2026". The ministry says "at the beginning of February at the latest"; in practice it has been published at the end of January. One call covers the University of Ljubljana, the University of Maribor, the University of Primorska, the University of Nova Gorica and the accredited independent institutions, so it sets the same application periods for all of them. Until the call is out, the deadlines for your cycle do not formally exist, and neither does the number of places nor any cap on entry (omejitev vpisa).

deadlines.label: First application period (prvi prijavni rok) — the one that matters
deadlines.audience: Slovenian citizens, EU citizens, and Slovenes abroad
deadlines.notes: Precedent, from the University of Ljubljana's Slovene VPIS leaflet for 2026: "Prijava v prvem roku: od 18. februarja do 18. marca 2026". You apply electronically through the eVS portal at portal.evs.gov.si using an electronic identity or an SI-PASS account, and you may name up to three study programmes in order of preference — the order decides which one you get if you clear the points threshold for more than one. The window closes in March, four months before IB results, so you apply on predicted grades and rank your three choices before you know what you scored. Any cap on entry (omejitev vpisa) is decided by 25 March and the number of applications per programme is published the same day, so you learn how competitive your choice was only after you are committed to it.

deadlines.label: First application period, the separate non-EU timetable
deadlines.audience: citizens of countries outside the EU
deadlines.notes: Precedent: the 2026/2027 non-EU handbook (rokovnik) was published on 27 January 2026, the first non-EU application period closed on 18 March 2026, and results followed on 27 August 2026 — a month later than the EU results. Applications go through the same eVS portal but the timetable and the contact differ; the University of Ljubljana routes non-EU applicants to admission@uni-lj.si rather than to the central VPIS office. One quirk runs the other way: the University of Ljubljana leaflet states that the English-taught Business and Economics degree at the Faculty of Economics may be chosen only in the non-EU rounds and by Slovenes abroad, so an EU applicant cannot select it in the ordinary EU round at all.

deadlines.label: Have every document in by this day, or your decision slips from July to September
deadlines.notes: It is the least visible date in the Slovenian cycle, and the one that costs a term. The University of Ljubljana leaflet, in Slovene: "V prvem roku: do 24. julija 2026 za vse, ki bodo do 10. julija 2026 oddali vsa zahtevana dokazila in imeli izdano odlocitev o priznanju tuje izobrazbe." In plain terms, you are included in the first-round decision of 24 July only if all your evidence is in by 10 July. IB results are released on about 6 July, which leaves roughly four days. Miss it and you are not rejected — you move to the "naknadno sprejeti" list decided by 18 September and then enrol by 30 September, after term has started. The good news for an IB student is in the same leaflet: the IB Diploma and the European Baccalaureate certificate are equivalent to the Slovenian matura and need no recognition procedure at all. That exemption is for the full Diploma; a candidate holding IB certificates rather than the Diploma must run the recognition procedure, and the leaflet warns a recognition decision can take up to two months from a complete application.

deadlines.label: Outer deadline for evidence in the first round, and for proving Slovene at B2
deadlines.audience: candidates finishing school in the same year; anyone who finished earlier submits by the March close instead
deadlines.notes: The leaflet, in Slovene: "V prvem prijavnem roku: letosnja generacija do 31. julija 2026. Kandidati, ki so ze koncali srednjesolsko izobrazevanje: do 18. marca 2026." The same 31 July is the deadline for evidence that you meet the enrolment conditions, which for almost every degree at the University of Ljubljana means a certificate of Slovene at B2 on the Common European Framework. Teaching is in Slovene; the B2 certificate is a separate examination taken at the Centre for Slovene as a Second and Foreign Language, and it is not something you arrange in the weeks after IB results.

deadlines.label: First-round selection result (sklep o rezultatu izbirnega postopka)
deadlines.notes: Precedent: 24 July 2026 for Slovenian and EU citizens whose evidence was complete by 10 July, 5 August 2026 for Slovenes abroad, 27 August 2026 for non-EU citizens, and 18 September 2026 for anyone admitted late in the first round. The decision is not posted to you: you read it by logging in to your own application at portal.evs.gov.si. Your enrolment window opens when it appears, and it is short.

deadlines.label: Enrolment (vpis) for everyone admitted in the first round — the place is not yours until you do this
deadlines.notes: The leaflet, in Slovene: "Kandidati, ki so sprejeti v prvem roku, se vpisejo od 24. julija do najkasneje 14. avgusta 2026; naknadno sprejeti do 30. septembra 2026; sprejeti v drugem prijavnem roku in v roku za zapolnitev mest do 30. septembra 2026." The first-round window is about three weeks across late July and early August, it runs straight through the Danish summer holidays, and enrolment happens at the faculty rather than centrally — "Vpis poteka na fakultetah in akademijah", which contact you in writing or by e-mail. Plan to be reachable, and to be able to get to Ljubljana in the first half of August if your faculty asks you to come in person.

deadlines.label: Second application period (drugi prijavni rok) — only for places left over
deadlines.notes: Precedent: "Prijava v drugem roku: od 20. do 27. avgusta 2026", with the list of remaining places published on 19 August 2026, results on 21 September 2026 and enrolment by 30 September 2026. Only for programmes with places left after the first round, and the popular ones will not be on the list. The leaflet also limits who may use it: candidates who did not apply in the first round, who were accepted nowhere in it, who did not enrol by 14 August, or whose first-round selection had not concluded. Non-EU citizens run a separate second period — 2 and 3 September 2026 in the 2026/2027 cycle — which individual faculties handle rather than the central VPIS office.

deadlines.label: Final round to fill any places still empty (rok za zapolnitev prostih vpisnih mest)
deadlines.notes: Precedent: "Prijava v roku za zapolnitev se prostih vpisnih mest: od 23. do 24. septembra 2026 do 10. ure", with the remaining places published on 22 September 2026 after 15:00, results by 25 September and enrolment by 30 September. Note the time of day: the window closes at 10:00 on the second morning, not at midnight, and evidence must be in by the same 10:00. One application, naming one programme, a week before term starts.

deadlines.label: Maribor, Primorska and Nova Gorica — the same national periods, not separate ones
deadlines.notes: Maribor, Primorska and Nova Gorica do not set their own application deadlines: gov.si states that undergraduate and integrated master’s admission at Ljubljana, Maribor, Primorska, Nova Gorica and the accredited independent institutions runs through one joint call, so the periods above are the national ones and apply to all of them. What does differ per university is the list of programmes, the number of places, any cap on entry, and the enrolment appointments, which each faculty arranges itself. The dates here are taken from the University of Ljubljana VPIS leaflet.

steps: Wait for the joint call for enrolment (skupni razpis za vpis) for your year. It has been published at the end of January two years running and it sets the deadlines, the programmes and the number of places.
Create a SI-PASS login and open an application in the eVS portal at portal.evs.gov.si.
Apply in the first period, which closed on 18 March in the 2026/2027 cycle. Name up to three programmes in order of preference - the order decides which one you get.

Ask the faculty in writing whether your IB Diploma needs a recognition decision. If it does, start it immediately: a decision can take two months and the July selection round only covers candidates who already hold one.

Get every document uploaded within days of IB results. In the 2026/2027 cycle the cut-off for the 24 July decision was 10 July; the outer deadline for that year’s school-leavers was 31 July, and so was the deadline for proving Slovene at B2.
If you are admitted on the July decision, enrol at the faculty itself before the mid-August deadline. Being selected is not being enrolled, and the enrolment window is about three weeks long.
application.selectionNotes: Programmes with more applicants than places apply "omejitev vpisa" - an enrolment limitation - and rank applicants on points. Whether a cap applies is decided by 25 March, after the March application deadline has already closed, and the number of applications per programme is published the same day, so you commit to your three choices before you know how competitive they are. The exact points formula, and how IB grades are converted into it, is set out in each faculty’s razpis for the relevant year. No separate application fee for eVS is published.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Very limited. About 17 English-taught bachelor programmes across the four public universities: University of Primorska 10 (Tourism; Tourism destination management; Anthropology; Cultural Heritage; Academic Bachelor in Management; Bioinformatics; Computer Science; Mathematics; Mathematics and Computer Science; Wood Innovation for Sustainability); University of Maribor 5 (Contemporary Tourism Practices; Economic and business sciences; Business administration; Economic and Technical Logistics; System logistics); University of Nova Gorica 1 (Physics and Astrophysics); University of Ljubljana 1 (Business and Economics, which the 2026/2027 call opened only to non-EU citizens and Slovenes abroad). Colleges and private institutions add about fifteen more, among them Alma Mater Europaea (eight), the College of Management Bled, the Academy of Visual Arts, NOA and GEA College.
notes: Slovene is not required for the specific English-taught programmes listed, but it is required for the overwhelming majority of bachelor teaching in the country.
Whether IB English A or B counts as proof of English, and the IELTS/TOEFL thresholds, are not confirmed here. Check with each faculty for the programme you want.
The programme list above comes from the national Study in Slovenia portal rather than from each faculty, so confirm the programme still runs in English before applying.

tuitionEuEea.value: Free. The University of Ljubljana states there are 'No tuition fees for full-time bachelor's and master's studies' for Slovenian citizens and 'students from EU countries, Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein, and Norway'. University of Primorska confirms 'full-time study at the 1st and 2nd level of study is free from tuition fee'. University of Nova Gorica lists EUR 0.00 per year for full-time EU/Slovenian citizens. Part-time study is not free, even for EU citizens.
tuitionEuEea.year: 2025/2026 (Nova Gorica, stated explicitly); Ljubljana and Primorska pages undated

tuitionNonEu.value: Roughly EUR 2,000-11,000 a year for bachelor study depending on the programme, per the national portal. University of Primorska publishes EUR 2,400-3,750 a year, but that range is explicitly labelled 2021/2022 and is probably out of date. University of Nova Gorica publishes EUR 2,800-3,500 a year for 2025/2026, though its wording attaches that bracket to part-time study. University of Ljubljana publishes only faculty-specific PDF price lists. Treat all of these as indicative.
tuitionNonEu.year: National range undated; Primorska 2021/2022; Nova Gorica 2025/2026

costs.applicationFee: No application fee for eVS is published. University of Primorska charges a registration fee of approximately EUR 50 a year.

livingCostMonthly.value: Roughly EUR 400-650 a month. Student dormitory EUR 120-250; a double room in a private flat EUR 150-200; a single room EUR 200-350. Subsidised student meals: the state contributes EUR 2.63 and you pay up to EUR 4.37. Public transport: EUR 1.50 for a 90-minute ticket, EUR 25 for a monthly student pass.
livingCostMonthly.year: Undated on the source page (as of September 2026)

notes: The subsidised student meal scheme ('studentski boni') is a real, significant saving and is one of the things that makes Slovenia cheap to live in.
The free-tuition rule applies to full-time study only. If you end up studying part-time you will pay, EU citizen or not.

funding: Ad futura international mobility scholarships, administered nationally.
A Public Call for Scholarships for Foreign Citizens exists but is aimed at Western Balkan postgraduate students, so it is unlikely to help an IB applicant from an EU/EEA country.
There is no general merit scholarship aimed at EU bachelor applicants - the funding story in Slovenia is that tuition is free, not that scholarships are plentiful.

funding.note: The programme must be SU-approved, and outside the Nordics SU is capped at four years (48 klip).

workRights: Slovenia has an unusual system called studentsko delo - student work through official Student Services, using a referral document ('napotnica'). Minimum referenced pay is EUR 7.21 an hour, with a 15.5% pension and disability deduction for all students, leaving about EUR 6.20. Foreign students additionally have 22.5% withheld as income tax prepayment, reclaimable if your home country has a double taxation treaty with Slovenia. Weekly or monthly hour limits, and any EU/non-EU eligibility difference, are not published with these rates; ask Student Services before you count on the income.
residency: As an EU/EEA citizen you must get a residence registration certificate within your first three months, applied for at the local administrative unit. You need a signed application, a biometric photo, a valid passport or ID, proof of address, proof of admission, proof of financial means of at least EUR 494.09 a month, and health insurance (EHIC). Fees are EUR 9.10 registration, EUR 4.50 application and EUR 12.32 for card printing, and renewal is typically by 30 September each year. Non-EU students must obtain a temporary residence permit before entering Slovenia, through a Slovenian diplomatic mission, and should get a police clearance certificate before travelling.
housing: This is the practical catch. Study in Slovenia states plainly that 'If you are coming as a private international student, unfortunately you do not have the option of staying in university student dormitories, except in Maribor' - the dorms are mainly reserved for exchange and scholarship students. In Ljubljana, dorm places where available are first-come-first-served at EUR 80-160 a month for a double room. Maribor opens applications after acceptance and emails information in July for the first semester; cost EUR 540-850 a semester. Primorska (around EUR 190 a month shared) and Nova Gorica (EUR 120-170 a month) send accommodation information about a month before the semester starts. Budget for the private market.
healthcare: As an EU/EEA citizen you are covered for necessary care with an EHIC. Students without EU/EEA or bilateral-agreement cover must buy compulsory Slovenian health insurance at EUR 126.33 a month (8.2% of average gross earnings), and the national portal recommends supplementary private insurance on top because the compulsory cover is only partial.

institutions.name: University of Ljubljana
institutions.englishBachelors: One: Business and Economics at the School of Economics and Business - but the 2026/2027 call let it be chosen only in the non-EU rounds and by Slovenes abroad, not in the EU round.
institutions.note: Teaches its bachelor's in Slovene; an EU applicant wanting its one English programme, Business and Economics, should ask the faculty first.

institutions.name: University of Maribor
institutions.englishBachelors: Five confirmed: Contemporary Tourism Practices; Economic and business sciences; Business administration; Economic and Technical Logistics; System logistics
institutions.note: Five English-taught bachelor's confirmed, and Study in Slovenia says a "private international student" cannot stay in university dormitories "except in Maribor".

institutions.name: University of Primorska
institutions.englishBachelors: Ten: Tourism; Tourism destination management; Anthropology; Cultural Heritage; Academic Bachelor in Management; Bioinformatics; Computer Science; Mathematics; Mathematics and Computer Science; Wood Innovation for Sustainability
institutions.note: On the Adriatic coast and the one Slovenian university with a real English-taught bachelor offering, especially in maths and computing through its FAMNIT faculty.

institutions.name: University of Nova Gorica
institutions.note: Tiny and research-intensive, on the Italian border, with an unusual School for Viticulture and Enology.

institutions.name: Alma Mater Europaea
institutions.englishBachelors: Eight identified: Archives Management; Physiotherapy; Humanities; Business Management; Dance/Choreography; Social Gerontology; Web and Information Technologies; Nursing
institutions.note: Private, with eight English-taught bachelor programmes identified - but private means you pay, so check the fee.

institutions.name: GEA College
institutions.englishBachelors: Entrepreneurship confirmed on the national English-programmes list; other programmes advertised but not cross-confirmed
institutions.note: A small private business school with a large network of partner institutions; describes itself as boutique. GEA's site is in Slovenian; its only substantial English page is the incoming-students page linked here, which is written for exchange students rather than for degree applicants. A degree applicant should expect to correspond in Slovenian or to write to the international office first.

institutions.name: International School for Social and Business Studies
institutions.englishBachelors: Not established: its two bachelor's (Economics in Contemporary Society; Business in Contemporary Society) are described in English but no teaching language is stated, and neither is on the national list of English-taught programmes.
institutions.note: Small private business faculty in Celje with Erasmus+ links. Applications go through the national eVŠ portal; whether the two bachelor programmes are taught in English is not stated on its undergraduate page, so ask before applying.
